title: Navigation updates: Profile header button, Logout in Settings, add Reel route

requirements.summary: Change the authenticated header primary action from Logout to Profile navigation while keeping Login behavior when unauthenticated.
acceptanceCriteria: When logged out, the header button label is "Login" and it triggers login.
When logged in, the header button label is "Profile" and it navigates to /profile.
Clicking the header button while logged in does not log the user out.

file_operations.description: Update the primary header button so unauthenticated state remains "Login" and triggers the Internet Identity login flow, while authenticated state shows "Profile" and navigates to "/profile" (no logout). Use the existing Internet Identity + logout patterns from the authorization component integration; Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Ensure Logout remains only in the Settings dropdown and still clears identity and React Query cache.
acceptanceCriteria: When logged in, the Settings dropdown contains a menu item labeled "Logout".
Clicking "Logout" in Settings logs the user out and clears client-side cached data as it did previously.
There is no other Logout control shown in the header outside of Settings.

file_operations.description: Keep a Settings (gear) dropdown item labeled "Logout" that executes the existing logout behavior (clear Internet Identity + clear React Query cache). Ensure the header primary button is no longer a Logout control. Use the existing logout/cache-clearing approach aligned with the authorization component guidance; Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Add a Reel item after Video in bottom navigation and create a /reel route with a placeholder Reel page.
acceptanceCriteria: Bottom navigation shows items in an order where "Reel" appears directly after "Video".
/reel renders a placeholder page with English text indicating the feature is coming soon.
The Reel nav item shows an active state when the current path is /reel.

file_operations.description: Insert a new primary nav item labeled "Reel" immediately after the existing "Video" item and ensure route-aware active styling works when the current path is "/reel".

Create a Reel placeholder page under frontend/src/pages with English user-facing text indicating the Reel feed is coming soon, matching the overall structure/visual pattern of the existing Video placeholder page.
Register a new route at path "/reel" that renders the new Reel page, and wire the page import into the existing router configuration.
